assessment: The incumbent delivered every ordered design and achieved 25–31 minutes for unadjusted small covers. Its fitting check catches repairable defects, but seven seam reworks and a 37-minute median suggest preventable work without establishing its duration or cause. Rework concentrated in large covers (5/8 versus 2/14 medium); a common allowance is a plausible contributor, not a demonstrated cause. The concrete limiting observation is that both unsuccessful observed customer placements involved rounded corners missing from the reference tables: passing those tables cannot establish customer fit. Reported waste is below 8%, but its weight-based estimate does not establish area compliance.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may produce a size-dependent finished-fit error that a sew-before-bulk-cut checkpoint could detect and reduce.
openings.delta: Measure the transfer from cutting-card dimensions to finished dimensions before committing the remaining purchased stock.
openings.prediction: If allowance is responsible, comparable pieces should show a repeatable signed dimensional error by size; errors clustering instead by operator, direction or design would weaken that account.
openings.probe: Sew the first ordered cover of each size before bulk cutting. Record cut and sewn dimensions, operator, grain direction, design, fitting error and stage times. Measure retained offcuts along both axes through the stipulated wash test. Trial a revised allowance only if supported; verify remaining layouts by area against 8% waste before recutting.
assumptions: Checkpoint effort fits the three-week window and 350-unit budget.
Early covers provide diagnostic evidence, not proof of batch-wide performance.

openings.claim: Does corner geometry explain customer placement failures independently of tabletop length and width?
openings.delta: Test whether the reference-table check misses a geometry-specific installation requirement.
openings.prediction: A cover that passes the reference check but fails on a similarly dimensioned rounded table would distinguish geometry mismatch from nominal size mismatch.
openings.probe: Use the six willing customers to obtain actual dimensions and corner profiles, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Compare first placement on reference and customer tables with similar dimensions and different corners; record where adjustment is needed. Use any supported pocket revision only after checking ordered appearance, removability and five-cycle wash survival.
assumptions: Participating customers include informative corner profiles and can demonstrate placement before dispatch.
Two observed failures do not establish corner shape as their cause.
